title: Someone follows you through the server room door
symptom: A person you do not recognise walks in behind you as you badge into the server room
user_description: Just a heads up: a man in a jacket was waiting by the server room door and walked in right behind you when you used your badge. He said he's here to fix the internet. I didn't see him sign in at reception.

options.text: Hold the door for him, he is probably a contractor
options.why: Following someone through a secure door without using your own badge is called tailgating. Anyone can claim to be a contractor.

options.text: Give him the door code so he does not have to wait for you next time
options.why: Never share door codes. It gives server room access to someone who has not been checked.

options.text: Ignore it, security is not your job
options.why: Everyone helps keep secure rooms secure. A stranger in the server room could steal or damage equipment and data.

options.text: Politely stop him and ask for his visitor badge or who he is visiting; do not let him stay without authorisation, take him to reception, and report it to the security team
options.why: Being polite but firm keeps the room safe. Reception can check if the visit is real, and security needs to know about tailgating.

hints: How can you check if a visitor is expected?
real_world_tip: Real contractors expect to sign in and be escorted. Asking to see a visitor badge is normal and polite, not rude.

escalation.team_why: The security team handles access to secure rooms. They can check door logs and camera footage and remind staff about tailgating.

details.text: The time and which door it happened at
details.why: Lets them check the door logs and cameras.

details.text: A description of the person and what he said
details.why: Helps them identify him and check whether the visit was real.

details.text: What you did (for example took him to reception)
details.why: Shows whether he is still in the building and who has seen him.

details.text: Your own badge number and PIN
details.why: Never share your badge PIN. The security team can look up your badge without it.
